newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open 0.40-0.50-cent lower.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open 0.40-0.50-cent lower.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open lower on Friday, following weakness in the early London market.
COMEX September was seen opening 0.40-0.50 cents down from Thursday's close of 108.10 cents a lb, after trading in a 107.60-108.25-cent range in ACCESS trade.

London Metal Exchange stocks increased another 2,925 tonnes in Friday's report to 248,700 tonnes, the highest level since Septemner 23, 1996. COMEX copper stocks declined 627 short tons to 32,434 tons.
The LME three-month price fell $51 overnight to $2,313 a tonne at 0751 EDT, but is still holding above support at $2,300. The cash-to-three-month backwardation was steady to firmer at $30.

Fundamentally, the market remains quiet with Europe in the midst of its summer shutdown period. Asian demand is believed by many to be lax. Demand is firm in the U.S., but dealers report more than ample supplies and expect warehouse stocks increase throughout the rest of the year.
